inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 502,664,337 issued less 8,480,644 treasury (incl. 2,631,462 BIP-trust shares) = 494.18m outstanding at 2026-03-31, plus 1,550k dilutive effect per the FY2026 diluted-EPS table (weighted diluted 495,738k). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (and is immaterial anyway); no non-SBC issuance planned.
inputs.sbc_source: Audited Financial Report FY2026 note 34(3): equity-settled share-based payment expense JPY 179m (FY2025: JPY 201m), BIP trust + stock options for directors/executive officers. No net-share-settlement taxes disclosed. At 0.016% of revenue this is an SBC-zero market: the projected sbc_pct_path is held at 0.0 (JPY 0.2bn is below modelling resolution) so house and street bases coincide and band_position is null by construction; the row is kept explicit per house rule.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in FY2024-FY2026 (treasury shares rose only via BIP-trust purchases). Flat count is a modelling convention, not funded by buybacks -- immaterial because SBC is JPY 0.2bn.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. 10y JGB ~1.7% (Oct-2026) + 6.0% ERP x beta ~1.15 = cost of equity ~8.6%; cost of debt 3.3% pre-tax (JPY 10,983m interest on ~JPY 330bn bonds+borrowings), ~2.3% after tax. At market weights (equity ~JPY 330bn, net debt JPY 219bn) the mechanical WACC is ~6.1%, which is also management's own 6% ROIC hurdle. House uses 7.5%: the mechanical figure gives perpetual credit for a debt-heavy structure management is explicitly committed to unwinding (deleveraging is a Corporate Plan 2026-2028 priority), and the house reference for JPY industrials is ~9%. 7.5% sits between the two. The SAME WACC is used in all three scenarios -- cyclicality, tariff and execution risk are charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Full lease cash charged inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path: FY2026 repayments of lease liabilities JPY 21,557m (financing) + interest expense on lease liabilities JPY 2,268m = JPY 23,825m = 2.19% of revenue. Lease liabilities (JPY 68,671m at 2026-03-31: 19,962 current + 48,709 non-current) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is bonds + borrowings only. D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: 58,683 - 18,519 = JPY 40,164m (3.7% of revenue). Lease cost glides 2.1% -> 2.0% because the Tokyo Hino land lease (ROU land JPY 33.7bn -> 7.3bn) was bought back in FY2026 and no longer carries a lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; non-controlling interests of JPY 12,466m (2026-03-31) are deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI share of FY2026 profit was JPY 1,568m (~5%), so an attributable-only leakage driver would be within noise.
inputs.non_operating_assets: Investment securities at fair value JPY 26,396m at 2026-03-31 (Level 1 JPY 23,430m; down from 45,293m after the JPY 21.2bn partial sale of Tempus AI shares received for Ambry Genetics). Added in the equity bridge because their dividend/fair-value income sits in finance income, outside EBITDA (matching-asset rule). Equity-method investments (JPY 1.0bn) and net retirement benefit liabilities are not bridged -- both immaterial at this scale.
inputs.capex_note: FY2026 reported capex JPY 61,102m (PPE 47,915 + intangibles 13,187) includes the one-off acquisition of real estate trust beneficiary interests in the Tokyo Site Hino land, previously sold-and-leased-back (ROU land fell JPY 26.4bn; lease liabilities fell JPY 26.2bn). Underlying capex ~JPY 35bn (3.2%); FY2024-FY2025 ran 3.7-3.9%. Base uses 3.8%, slightly above D&A ex-ROU, for Industry capacity (SANUQI/SAZMA films, DUV optical components, IJ printheads).
inputs.fcf_base_note: reported_fcf = OCF 86,286 - capex 61,102 = 25,184 (CSV definition; the company's own 'free cash flow' of 52.2bn adds investing inflows incl. the Tempus share sale and is not used). Under IFRS the company books interest paid (JPY 10,828m) and interest received (2,969m) inside operating activities, so reported FCF is a LEVERED figure. The projection is component-built from EBITDA and is unlevered, with net debt subtracted in the bridge; last_fcf is recorded for audit and CAGR purposes only. interest_income is 0 because the company is net-debt (JPY 219bn), so no cash pile is double-counted.
inputs.precision_medicine_note: Ambry Genetics (sold to Tempus 2025-02-03) and Invicro (sold 2024-04-30) are discontinued operations. The Metrics CSV carries FY2024 and earlier as first reported (Precision Medicine inside revenue, ~JPY 90bn); FY2025 and FY2026 are continuing operations. FY2026 (JPY 1,087.7bn revenue) is a clean post-divestiture base and is what the growth path compounds from; historical revenue CAGRs across FY2024/FY2025 are depressed by the deconsolidation and are read accordingly.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, probability-weighted -- routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied (JPY-built WACC, single lease treatment B, NCI charged once in the bridge, investment securities bridged as the matching asset, SBC-zero market, risk charged once). Konica Minolta is an operating industrial (office MFPs / production print / sensing-materials-optics / healthcare imaging) whose value is a stream of free cash flow; none of the non-FCF routes apply. FY2026 is treated as a recovery year rather than a run-rate: EBITDA margin 10.0% reported (10.3% on business-contribution-profit basis) versus 10.5-11.5% in FY2016-FY2019 before the Precision Medicine impairments and COVID; the base path takes management's FY2027 guidance at face value (revenue +1.6%, OP flat at JPY 50bn) and then reaches a 6.0% business-contribution ratio rather than the 6.5% FY2028 target, given the missed 2023-2025 plan. Price is the 2026-10-30 TSE regular close (not after-hours). Balance sheet and share count are both from the 2026-03-31 annual (latest filing; the H1 FY2027 interim to 2026-09-30 is not yet in the folder -- refresh net debt when it lands).

equity_bridge.note: Audited FY2026 note 35, 2026-03-31; matching asset for finance income excluded from EBITDA
Consolidated balance sheet 2026-03-31; flows are consolidated so NCI is deducted once here

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 revenue guidance (JPY 1,105bn vs 1,087.7bn actual); management's 3% FY2025-FY2028 CAGR is used only as the bull anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR +3.3% vs revenue 3yr CAGR -1.3% (revenue depressed by the Precision Medicine deconsolidation; equity depressed by FY2023 and FY2025 losses) -- neither is a usable forward anchor, hence guidance is selected.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF less JPY ~0.2bn SBC (immaterial, so owner and reported CAGRs coincide). EPS and 3yr FCF CAGRs are undefined: FY2023 FCF was -27.5bn and EPS was negative in FY2021-FY2023 and FY2025. 5yr owner-FCF CAGR -7.8% runs FY2021 (37.9bn) to FY2026 (25.2bn), the latter after the one-off Hino land purchase; on underlying capex FY2026 FCF would be ~51bn. Revenue: FY2023 1,130.4bn -> FY2026 1,087.7bn; FY2021 863.4bn (COVID trough) -> FY2026. Equity: FY2023 487.4bn -> FY2026 536.5bn; FY2021 539.9bn -> FY2026.

base.narrative: FY2027 as guided (revenue +1.6% to ~1,105bn, OP ~50bn), then revenue grows ~2-2.5% for three years as Industry (+9% target, modelled ~6-7%) and Professional Print offset a ~1-2%/yr office decline, fading to 1% as the office base keeps shrinking. EBITDA margin (post-IFRS-16, pre-lease-cost) 10.3% -> 11.0% by FY2030 and flat thereafter -- equivalent to a ~6.0% business-contribution ratio, short of the 6.5% FY2028 target. Lease cost 2.1% -> 2.0%, D&A ex-ROU 3.7% -> 3.6%, capex 3.8%, cash tax 28% for two years (DTA utilisation) then 30% as management guides. Working capital consumes 15% of each year's revenue increase (inventories JPY 208bn + receivables exceed payables). Terminal: 1.0% growth, 12x cap on a cyclical.

bull.narrative: Corporate Plan 2026-2028 delivered: revenue CAGR ~3.5% (Industry at the 9% target on SANUQI/SAZMA film capacity, DUV optical components and IJ printheads; DW-DX recurring services offset office hardware decline; production print digital shift), tariff refunds and mitigation recover most of the JPY 12bn gross-profit hit, and the 6.5% business-contribution ratio is reached by FY2028 and extended to ~6.8% as the ROIC framework prunes low-return lines. EBITDA margin reaches 12.3%. Capex runs 4% through the capacity build. Terminal 1.5% growth, 13x cap. Same 7.5% WACC -- the upside lives in the flows.

bear.narrative: The 2026-2028 plan goes the way of 2023-2025: office print volumes fall faster than DW-DX monetises, Industry customers (display, auto, semiconductor) keep deferring capex, Imaging Solutions stays loss-making, and U.S. tariffs stay at 15-22.5% with no refund. Revenue slips ~1-1.5%/yr for five years then flattens; EBITDA margin erodes to 9.0% (business-contribution ratio ~4%), i.e. back to the FY2024 level rather than a new impairment cycle. Capex held to 3.5% to protect cash, tax 30% throughout. Working-capital release on shrinking revenue partly cushions FCF. Terminal 0% growth, 10x cap. Leverage (JPY 219bn net debt, 60% of market cap) is what makes this path painful per share.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance-level FY2027, then a modest, below-plan recovery: ~2% revenue growth and an 11% EBITDA margin (~6% business-contribution ratio) by FY2030, with Industry growth roughly offsetting the office decline. Terminal 1%, 12x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: Corporate Plan 2026-2028 delivered and extended: Industry at its 9% growth target, DW-DX offsetting office decline, tariff mitigation and refunds, 6.5%+ business-contribution ratio, EBITDA margin 12.3%. Terminal 1.5%, 13x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: Targets missed again: office decline outruns DW-DX, Industry capex deferrals persist, tariffs unrecovered; revenue shrinks ~1-1.5%/yr to FY2031, EBITDA margin back to 9%. Terminal 0%, 10x cap, leverage amplifies the per-share hit.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: half of revenue (Digital Workplace) is in an acknowledged secular decline, the 2023-2025 plan missed its own 'strengthening businesses' targets, Imaging Solutions is still loss-making after years of restructuring, tariffs are outside management's control, and net debt is ~60% of market cap so a flat-to-shrinking operating case bites hard per share. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right at once (Industry hitting a 9% CAGR, DW-DX genuinely offsetting office decline, and tariff recovery). Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Konica Minolta is valued as a levered, slow-growth industrial in the middle of a credible but unproven turnaround. The model deliberately refuses to extrapolate either the FY2025 trough (impairments and restructuring) or the FY2026 recovery year, anchoring instead on FY2027 guidance and a mid-cycle margin below management's FY2028 target. Leases are charged as an operating cost (treatment B), NCI is deducted once, investment securities including the residual Tempus stake are bridged in, and risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights rather than in a per-scenario discount rate. The terminal value is capped at 10-13x FCF because the market has never paid a compounder multiple for this franchise and the office base is shrinking.
key_risks_to_valuation: Office MFP volume decline faster than the 1-2%/yr embedded in the base; Digital Workplace is ~56% of revenue
Execution on Corporate Plan 2026-2028 after missed 2023-2025 targets; base already haircuts the 6.5% business-contribution target to ~6.0%
U.S. tariffs (JPY 12.2bn gross FY2026 hit, 5.3bn net) and the uncertain USD 47.6m refund, excluded from guidance
FX: plan built on JPY 150/USD and 180/EUR; a stronger yen cuts translated revenue and margin
Leverage: JPY 219bn net debt (ex-leases) against a ~JPY 330bn market cap means each 1pp of EBITDA margin is worth roughly JPY 15-20/share and the bear case lands well below half the base
Industry Business cyclicality (display, automotive, semiconductor customer capex) -- the only growth engine in the base case
Deferred-tax-asset recoverability drives reported profit swings; the model uses a 28-30% cash rate, not the FY2026 effective rate
H1 FY2027 (to 2026-09-30) results are not yet in the folder; net debt and guidance should be refreshed when they land
